early_baseline_provenance: USGS approximate 2015–2025 annual averages: about 110 magnitude 6.0–6.9, 13 magnitude 7.0–7.9 and 0.7 magnitude 8+ earthquakes; annual counts and clustering vary.
forecast_method: stationary independent Poisson weekly count BASELINE, using an approximate 52 weeks/year; no information from after created_at_utc; p deliberately rounded; cannot forecast individual earthquakes or risks.

questions.question: At least one worldwide USGS event with magnitude >= 7.0 and UTC time in [2026-11-02T00:00:00Z,2026-11-09T00:00:00Z)?
At least three worldwide USGS events with magnitude >= 6.0 and UTC time in [2026-11-02T00:00:00Z,2026-11-09T00:00:00Z)?

resolution_rule: After 2026-11-23T00:00:00Z, query USGS authoritative event catalog with strict UTC [start,end) filtering; count unique events, inclusive minmagnitude; record query and retrieved event IDs; cases of missing or inconsistent data remain unresolved.
caveats: The Poisson assumption ignores aftershocks and temporal clustering; forecasts are simplistic statistical baselines, not hazard warnings.
Independent oracle verification, calibration and measured curiosity gain are not established by publishing a forecast.
Both questions share the same underlying earthquakes, so statistical dependence matters.
This is a public preregistration proof-of-concept; branch history can be rewritten; immutable-commit URL must be referenced in subsequent submissions.
